decision: Introduce a thin ExecutionBackend interface (spawn/attach/list/stop/suspend/resume returning an IPty-shaped stream) with the existing node-pty docker/host-shell path moved verbatim into a `container` backend (default) and an opt-in `substrate` backend behind DAAX_SUBSTRATE_ENABLED.
rationale: Owner decision on dx#113: use substrate primitives, no daax-side runtime or scheduler. Everything above the PTY already depends only on IPty, so a backend that yields an IPty keeps the UI, WS protocol, recorder and ticket auth unchanged. The flag keeps galway/muckross and both deployment modes on today's behaviour.
alternatives: A separate substrate service called by daax-terminal (rejected by the dx#113 decision); a nanofuse-shaped runtime layer (never built, explicitly rejected).

decision: Split substrate responsibilities by plane: the web plane (has Postgres) owns lifecycle and the substrate_sessions store; the terminal plane only attaches, authorized by a single-use WS ticket carrying a `substrate {session, actor}` claim minted by POST /api/substrate/sessions/:id/attach after the owner check.
rationale: The split deploy's terminal service has no Postgres (lib/host-shell-access.ts, F3). Reusing the existing HMAC ticket keeps one credential path and lets the terminal server trust the actor named in a signed claim without a store. Forwarded-identity upgrades without a ticket are refused for substrate because this plane cannot check ownership; the host-dev loopback operator (admin-equivalent) may attach by session+actor.
alternatives: Give daax-terminal DATABASE_URL (widens its privileges, contradicts F3); a separate attach token format (duplicate crypto); trusting query params (no authorization).

decision: Substrate sessions are persistent: a WS close detaches only (no EOF, no SIGTERM, no actor call); there are no idle or disconnect timeouts; End session (delete egress policy, then actor) is the only kill; suspend/resume are explicit routes; attach never auto-resumes (409 when suspended).
rationale: Owner decision on dx#114. Detach-only also removes the 1 s typed-command race: the agent is the template's entrypoint (AGENT env) and nothing is typed into a substrate PTY.
alternatives: Suspend on disconnect / idle timeout (rejected by the dx#114 decision).

decision: One upstream ptyd stream per session in the terminal server, fanned out to all attached viewers; recording is done once at that hub, keyed by the daax session id, and is not stopped on detach (flushed instead), so it continues across reattaches. The local `kubectl ate proxy actor` tunnel closes when the last viewer leaves.
rationale: Recordings must continue across reattaches (dx#114) without duplicate captures from multiple tabs. Closing the local port forward when unused costs one tunnel restart on reattach and keeps no per-session kubectl process alive indefinitely; it never affects the actor. Known limit: output produced while no viewer is attached is not recorded, and a terminal-server restart starts a new recording file for the session.
alternatives: Keep an upstream stream open while detached to record unattended output (one long-lived kubectl process per session, indefinitely); per-WS recordings (duplicates, breaks continuity).

decision: Transport `proxy` uses `kubectl ate proxy actor <n> <port>:80 -a <atespace>` with a GET /healthz readiness wait and the ptyd WS contract (/pty, binary PTY bytes, JSON text control); `router` is a documented stub until placement is decided.
rationale: The proxy path goes through the substrate router and is proven in substrate-harness (harness/terminal.go). Placement of daax-terminal relative to the cluster (dx#115/#121) is undecided, so direct router access is left as an interface.
alternatives: Direct pod dialing (bypasses the router; refused by substrate-harness design); building router access now (premature).

decision: Per-session EgressPolicy is default-deny plus the LLM gateway http rule, an optional Watchtower hook gateway route (placeholder, only when DAAX_SUBSTRATE_WATCHTOWER_HOOK_URL is set), user-selected presets (npm, PyPI, GitHub) and validated extra hosts as TLS passthrough :443; host validation is ported from substrate-harness harness/egress.go.
rationale: Owner decision on dx#118: each exception is an explicit, reviewed route, never a private-range opening. Porting the harness validation keeps one policy for IP literals, internal suffixes, rebinding domains, over-broad wildcards and private resolution.
alternatives: Opening daax-net ranges to actors (rejected: the lockdown exists because an actor reached kube-apiserver via a rebinding name).

decision: Cluster identity is explicit: DAAX_SUBSTRATE_KUBECONFIG (absolute) or DAAX_SUBSTRATE_IN_CLUSTER=1 is required, and the child env re-pins KUBECONFIG; the default ~/.kube/config is never used.
rationale: On kinsale ~/.kube/config is a different, real cluster; an implicit fallback could create or delete actors on the wrong cluster.
alternatives: kubectl's default resolution (unsafe on this host).

decision: A failed create tears down whatever it made (egress policy + actor) and leaves the session in `error`, which can only be ended, never resumed; a create that completes after End is cleaned up; only an explicit already-running reply counts as a successful resume.
rationale: Validation review: resuming an errored session could start an actor whose egress policy was never created, and End during provisioning could orphan an actor created after the delete. Loose 'running' substring matching treated 'not running' as success.
alternatives: Re-verify the policy on resume from error (more surface, same outcome as End + recreate).

decision: Users see a classified failure reason (timeout, capacity, unavailable, not authorized, generic); raw kubectl-ate stderr goes to the server log only. In-cluster mode pins KUBECONFIG=/dev/null.
rationale: Validation review: stderr can carry cluster endpoints, kubeconfig and token-file paths. client-go loads ~/.kube/config before the in-cluster fallback, so an unset KUBECONFIG was not enough on a host that has one. The in-cluster fallback with an empty KUBECONFIG is client-go behaviour not exercised here (no in-cluster run in this change).
alternatives: Returning stderr to admins only (still leaks via shared screens/logs); overriding HOME (breaks kubectl-ate caches).

decision: Supersedes part of substrate-backend-004: while a session is being recorded, its upstream stream (and local tunnel) stays open with zero viewers, so output produced while nobody is attached is recorded; without a recording the stream closes with the last viewer as before. End is allowed from every live state including suspending/resuming, and operation completions use guarded transitions so they cannot overwrite an End; a first-attempt actor-name collision is never cleaned up.
rationale: Codex cross-provider review round 1: recording gaps between attaches violated continuous recording (dx#114); a web restart mid-suspend/resume left an unkillable session; cleanup after a name collision could delete another session's actor.
alternatives: Keeping gaps (004 as written); a reconciler that repairs transitional states on boot (more machinery, End-from-any-state already gives the user a way out).

decision: An actor-name collision at create moves the still-creating session to a fresh name (guarded rename, up to 3 attempts); if every attempt collides the record is closed (ended) without any substrate call. A viewer's record request keeps the stream open across a detach even before the first output.
rationale: Codex review round 2: after a collision the error session still referenced the other actor, so a later End would delete it; and a detach before the first output dropped the recording stream.
alternatives: An owns_actor column checked by End (keeps a useless error record and a second ownership notion).

decision: Actor ownership is explicit: substrate_sessions.actor_owned is set by the spawn's onActorCreated callback the moment this session's create call makes the actor. End re-reads the row after moving it to `ending` and deletes the actor only when actor_owned is true; provisioning cleans up only what it created. A create still in flight when End runs sees the state change and removes what it made itself.
rationale: Codex review round 3: End during provisioning could call stop on a candidate name that belonged to someone else (collision not yet detected) or on a stale name read before a rename. Known residual: a web-plane crash between create success and the ownership write leaves an unowned daax-* actor (visible via list, never someone else's).
alternatives: A global per-session lock across planes (no shared lock exists between processes); deleting by name unconditionally (the bug).
